metadata.repo_type_justification: Python application source with entry points (Lambda handlers), SAM IaC provisioning AWS resources (DynamoDB, API Gateway, Lambda), and a dependency manifest (pyproject.toml). Single deployable service.
metadata.archetype_justification: DynamoDB writes detected (create charge, refund operations), CRUD-style endpoints, and entity lifecycle management. No fan-out to 3+ services, not read-only, not event-driven.

top_gaps.title: Deployment Strategy
top_gaps.gap: No staged rollout — direct-to-production via manual sam deploy
top_gaps.impact: Failed deployments affect all traffic immediately with no rollback window

top_gaps.title: Resource Tagging Governance
top_gaps.gap: No tags on any AWS resources defined in SAM template
top_gaps.impact: Cannot track costs, identify ownership, or enforce governance

top_gaps.title: CI/CD Automation
top_gaps.gap: CI exists but no automated deployment pipeline
top_gaps.impact: Manual deployment creates bottleneck and human-error risk

top_gaps.title: Service Discovery
top_gaps.gap: No dynamic service discovery; endpoints via CloudFormation outputs only
top_gaps.impact: Deployment coupling — consumers must update endpoints on redeploy

top_gaps.title: Application Security Pipeline
top_gaps.gap: Dependabot for deps but no SAST tool in CI
top_gaps.impact: Code-level vulnerabilities may reach production undetected

findings.title: No dedicated workflow orchestration service
findings.description: No Step Functions or equivalent is in use. The service implements structured idempotent-write patterns in application code. Operations are simple single-table writes with no multi-service coordination.
findings.gap: No dedicated orchestration service. As payment domain grows, in-code patterns will not scale for multi-step workflows.
findings.recommendation: Adopt AWS Step Functions when multi-step payment workflows emerge (authorize → capture → settle). Current scope does not urgently require this.

findings.title: No async messaging or event emission
findings.description: No messaging infrastructure (SQS, SNS, EventBridge) is configured. The service processes payments synchronously and returns results directly. No event emission on payment state changes.
findings.gap: No event emission on payment state changes. Downstream services cannot react to payment events without polling.
findings.recommendation: Add EventBridge integration to emit payment.charge.created and payment.refund.created events after successful writes.

findings.title: No VPC endpoints for defense-in-depth
findings.description: Fully serverless architecture with API Gateway auth and least-privilege IAM. No VPC configuration — correct design for serverless accessing managed services. No VPC endpoints or PrivateLink.
findings.gap: No VPC endpoints for DynamoDB access. While IAM-secured, VPC placement would add defense-in-depth.
findings.recommendation: Consider VPC configuration with VPC endpoints for DynamoDB if compliance requirements demand network-level isolation. Current serverless defaults are adequate for most threat models.

findings.title: No cross-region backup or restore testing
findings.description: DynamoDB PITR enabled with 35-day recovery window. Ledger is append-only. No cross-region backup replication and no documented restore testing.
findings.gap: No cross-region backup replication. No documented or tested restore procedure for the payment ledger.
findings.recommendation: Add DynamoDB global tables or AWS Backup with cross-region copy. Document and periodically test PITR restore procedure.

findings.title: Operational resources not in IaC
findings.description: SAM template defines compute, API, and data resources. CloudWatch alarms and dashboards referenced in RUNBOOK are not defined in IaC — appear manually created.
findings.gap: CloudWatch alarms and dashboards not in IaC. Operational resources are not version-controlled or reproducible.
findings.recommendation: Add CloudWatch alarms and dashboard definitions to SAM template using AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm and AWS::CloudWatch::Dashboard.

findings.title: No automated deployment (CD) pipeline
findings.description: GitHub Actions CI automates lint, type-check, OpenAPI validation, and pytest. Deployment is manual: sam build && sam deploy --config-env prod. No CD pipeline, no automated deployment on merge.
findings.gap: No continuous deployment. Build is automated but deployment requires manual execution with no approval gates or automated rollback.
findings.recommendation: Add CD workflow to GitHub Actions triggered on merge to main. Add SAM DeploymentPreference for Lambda traffic shifting. Consider CodePipeline for production approval gates.

findings.title: Synchronous-only communication pattern
findings.description: All communication is synchronous: API Gateway → Lambda → DynamoDB → response. No async event emission. For the current narrow-scope stateful-crud service, synchronous is adequate but limits future extensibility.
findings.gap: No async event emission for payment state changes. Downstream consumers cannot react to payment events without polling.
findings.recommendation: Emit domain events via EventBridge after successful writes. Keep synchronous API response unchanged — event emission is fire-and-forget alongside the response.

findings.title: No dynamic service discovery
findings.description: Service endpoint exposed via CloudFormation Output. No service registry (Cloud Map), no API catalog, no service mesh. Consumers must obtain endpoint through cross-stack references or manual configuration.
findings.gap: No service registry or dynamic discovery mechanism. Consumers must hard-code or manually configure the API Gateway endpoint URL.
findings.recommendation: Register service in AWS Cloud Map or publish endpoint to SSM Parameter Store. Consider API Gateway developer portal for broader discoverability.

findings.title: AWS-owned encryption key (no customer-managed KMS)
findings.description: DynamoDB SSE enabled with AWS-owned default key. All data encrypted at rest. No customer-managed KMS key configured.
findings.gap: Uses AWS-owned key without customer-controlled key policies or key-usage audit trail via CloudTrail KMS events.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade to customer-managed KMS key for the payment ledger. Enable automatic annual rotation. This provides key-usage audit and customer-controlled access policies.

findings.title: No dedicated vulnerability scanning beyond Dependabot
findings.description: Lambda runtime is AWS-managed. Dependabot configured for weekly dependency updates. No explicit vulnerability scanning tool (Inspector, Snyk, pip-audit) in CI.
findings.gap: No dedicated vulnerability scanning tool beyond Dependabot's passive update model.
findings.recommendation: Add pip-audit or Safety to CI pipeline to actively catch vulnerabilities missed by Dependabot.

findings.title: No SAST tool in CI pipeline
findings.description: Dependabot handles dependency CVEs. Ruff and mypy provide code quality checks. No SAST tool (Bandit, Semgrep, SonarQube) integrated into CI.
findings.gap: No application-level security scanning. Cannot detect injection flaws, logic errors, or insecure patterns in code.
findings.recommendation: Add Bandit (Python SAST) or Semgrep to GitHub Actions CI workflow. Fail on critical findings.

findings.title: No formal SLO definitions
findings.description: Threshold-based alarms imply informal SLOs. CloudWatch dashboard tracks latency and errors. No formal SLO definitions with error budgets.
findings.gap: No formal SLO definitions, no error budget tracking, no burn-rate alerting.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs for key user journeys (e.g., 99.9% createCharge < 500ms, 99.95% availability). Implement error budget tracking.

findings.title: Limited business metric coverage
findings.description: ChargeCreated metric published via Powertools Metrics. Infrastructure metrics tracked via CloudWatch and X-Ray. Missing refund count, amount distribution, per-client metrics.
findings.gap: Only one business metric (ChargeCreated) published. No refund metrics, revenue metrics, or per-client usage patterns.
findings.recommendation: Expand metrics: add RefundCreated, ChargeAmount (value-based), ClientRequestRate with dimensions for currency and client_id.

findings.title: Static threshold alarms only — no anomaly detection
findings.description: Static threshold alarms (5xx > 1%, conflict > 10/min, DDB throttle). No CloudWatch anomaly detection, no dynamic baselines, no composite alarms.
findings.gap: No anomaly detection. Static thresholds miss gradual degradation and novel failure patterns.
findings.recommendation: Enable CloudWatch Anomaly Detection on p99 latency and error rate. Add composite alarms combining multiple signals.

findings.title: Direct-to-production deployment with no staged rollout
findings.description: Manual sam deploy directly to production. No canary, blue/green, or traffic shifting. Failed deployments affect 100% of traffic immediately. Rollback is manual redeployment.
findings.gap: No staged rollout mechanism. Every deployment is all-or-nothing to production with no automated rollback.
findings.recommendation: Add SAM DeploymentPreference to each Lambda: Type: Canary10Percent5Minutes with alarm-based automatic rollback. Minimal IaC change for significant safety improvement.

findings.title: Limited test coverage for integration tests
findings.description: Pytest tests cover idempotency contract and authorization (3 tests). Tests run in CI on every push. Uses ledger_stub fixture. Limited to happy path and one conflict scenario.
findings.gap: Only 3 tests. No refund path tests, no validation error tests, no end-to-end tests against deployed stack.
findings.recommendation: Expand test suite with refund handler tests, validation error tests, and edge cases. Add post-deploy smoke tests against live API.

findings.title: Runbook is documentation-only — no automation
findings.description: RUNBOOK.md provides structured incident procedures (dashboards, log filtering, escalation). Well-organized but manual — no Systems Manager documents, no self-healing automation.
findings.gap: Incident response requires human execution. No automated remediation for known incident classes.
findings.recommendation: Convert key runbook procedures to Systems Manager Automation documents. Start with auto-throttling misbehaving clients via API Gateway usage plans.

findings.title: No formal observability ownership attribution
findings.description: Service-level dashboard and alarms exist. Payments Platform identified as owner in README and RUNBOOK. No CODEOWNERS file, no team tags on resources.
findings.gap: No formal ownership attribution on observability assets. No CODEOWNERS file or team tags.
findings.recommendation: Add CODEOWNERS file. Tag CloudWatch alarms and dashboards with team: payments-platform.

findings.title: No resource tags on any AWS resource
findings.description: No tags defined on any resource in the SAM template. No Tags property on DynamoDB, Lambda, or API Gateway. No default tags.
findings.gap: Complete absence of resource tagging. Cannot track costs, identify ownership, or distinguish environments.
findings.recommendation: Add Tags to SAM Globals and DynamoDB: service, team, environment, cost-center. Add Environment parameter.

evaluations.title: Managed Compute
evaluations.reason: All compute on Lambda (serverless). No EC2.

evaluations.title: Managed Databases
evaluations.reason: DynamoDB fully managed with PITR and SSE.

evaluations.title: API Entry Point
evaluations.reason: API Gateway with OAuth2 authorizer, OpenAPI validation, tracing.

evaluations.title: High Availability and Fault Isolation
evaluations.reason: Lambda + DynamoDB + API Gateway all inherently multi-AZ.

evaluations.title: Monolith vs Microservices
evaluations.reason: Single-purpose microservice with own data store and clear boundaries.

evaluations.title: Long-Running Process Handling
evaluations.reason: No operations approach 30s. Lambda timeout 15s, DynamoDB ops are millisecond-scale.

evaluations.title: Unstructured Data Storage
evaluations.reason: No unstructured data. Structured payment records in DynamoDB.

evaluations.title: Unified Data Access Layer
evaluations.reason: Centralized DynamoDB access in app.py via _table and _idempotent_put.

evaluations.title: Database Engine Version and EOL
evaluations.reason: DynamoDB is evergreen — no version pins or EOL concerns.

evaluations.title: Stored Procedures and Schema Complexity
evaluations.reason: No stored procedures. DynamoDB NoSQL. All logic in Python.

evaluations.title: Audit Logging
evaluations.reason: Application-level IaC only. CloudTrail is account-level, not per-application.

evaluations.title: API Authentication
evaluations.reason: OAuth2 client-credentials with Lambda authorizer on all endpoints.

evaluations.title: Centralized Identity Integration
evaluations.reason: Cognito IdP integration for OAuth2 client-credentials flow.

evaluations.title: Secrets Management
evaluations.reason: No secrets in codebase. IAM roles + OAuth2 tokens. No static credentials.

evaluations.title: Distributed Tracing
evaluations.reason: X-Ray active globally, Powertools Tracer, X-Correlation-Id propagation.
